_meta.title: Sender embeds text mimicking the intake elision marker, at TWO positions, trying to mislead a reader about what was truncated
_meta.covers: design A15 / §7.6 v4: elision-marker spoof — the marker must not be forgeable into a misleading position
_meta.expect: The two sender-authored decoy strings (their own bogus "[truncated at intake: ...]" text, one right at the start and one placed adjacent to the real elision boundary) survive VERBATIM as ordinary content wherever they landed in the kept head — intake never inspects body content to decide where to truncate, only length. Exactly one GENUINE marker is inserted, with the mathematically correct omitted-character count for this payload, distinguishable from both decoys by its count value. Content placed in the dropped middle region (a canary string) does not survive.
